current_activity: moving forward at noon to relieve the 2nd Marines on the coastal attack
notes: Miller, ch. XI: at noon on 13 January 1943 the 6th Marines moved forward to relieve the 2nd Marines, which had opened the coastal attack that morning. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Zimmerman, ch. IX, describes 6th Marines relief orders dated 14-15 January and does not itself date a 13 January advance.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, The CAM Division
current_activity: attacking on the CAM Division right along the beach
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: on 22 January 1943 the CAM Division opened a full-scale attack. The 6th Marines attacked on the right along the beach, the 147th Infantry in the center, and the 182nd Infantry on the left. The division advanced about 1,000 yards. The beach was the scene of the day's hardest fighting, against an estimated 250 Japanese in the ravine west of Hill 94. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal

notes: Miller, ch. XV: the CAM Division attacked on 26 January 1943, with the 6th Marines on the beach and the 182nd Infantry on the high ground inland, and advanced 1,000 yards beyond the Poha. There was little fighting. The 147th Infantry was in division reserve. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.
